think_cards.title: Playing with Friends
think_cards.scenario: You want to ride bikes, but your friend prefers to play video games.
think_cards.question: How can you combine both activities for fun?
think_cards.image_concept: A group of kids smiling as they ride their bikes together, with one child holding a portable video game console, suggesting they take turns biking and playing games under a tree.

think_cards.title: Choosing a Snack
think_cards.scenario: You want cookies, but your sibling wants fruit.
think_cards.question: What snack could satisfy both of you?
think_cards.image_concept: Two siblings sitting at a table with a plate of cookies and a bowl of fresh fruit, happily sharing the cookies while making fruit sandwiches together, creating a fun snack for both.

think_cards.title: Saturday Activities
think_cards.scenario: Your team wants to practice basketball while you want to go swimming.
think_cards.question: What could be a win-win plan for both your team and you?
think_cards.image_concept: A diverse group of kids at a park, one group practicing basketball on one side while another group sets up a small pool nearby, all laughing together as they plan to switch activities after a set time.

think_cards.title: Studying Together
think_cards.scenario: You want to study for a test, but your friend wants to watch a movie.
think_cards.question: How can you balance studying and having fun together?
think_cards.image_concept: Two friends sitting on a couch surrounded by study materials and popcorn, one writing notes while the other holds a remote, taking breaks to watch short clips from a movie they both enjoy.

sections.heading: What is Win-Win?
sections.body: Win-win thinking means finding solutions that are good for everyone involved. Instead of just one person winning, both can feel happy.
sections.image_concept: What is Win-Win?. Win-win thinking means finding solutions that are good for everyone involved. Instead of just one person winning, both can feel happy.

sections.heading: The Importance of Listening
sections.body: To create a win-win, listen to what others want. This shows you care about their feelings and needs.
sections.image_concept: The Importance of Listening. To create a win-win, listen to what others want. This shows you care about their feelings and needs.

sections.heading: Keeping Promises
sections.body: Trust is key in relationships. When you keep your promises, you build trust like adding to an emotional bank account.
sections.image_concept: Keeping Promises. Trust is key in relationships. When you keep your promises, you build trust like adding to an emotional bank account.

sections.heading: Making Agreements
sections.body: A win-win agreement helps partners understand how to work together. Clear steps make it easier for everyone to win.
sections.image_concept: Making Agreements. A win-win agreement helps partners understand how to work together. Clear steps make it easier for everyone to win.

quiz.question: What does win-win thinking mean?
quiz.why: Win-win thinking is about finding solutions where both sides are satisfied.

quiz.question: Why is listening important in win-win solutions?
quiz.why: Listening shows that you care about the other person's needs.

quiz.question: What builds trust in relationships?
quiz.why: When you keep your promises, you are making deposits in your emotional bank account.

quiz.question: What can lead to less fighting in relationships?
quiz.why: Win-win agreements help everyone understand each other and create harmony.

quiz.question: What can be a consequence of not keeping promises?
quiz.why: Failure to keep promises creates withdrawals in the emotional bank account, leading to less trust.
